title: Reading Drill — Comparing weaving samples — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Comparing weaving samples — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The textile tutor had been asked to investigate samples tightening differently when removed from a loom in Millcross. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on change in width, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a four-week comparison, the team used marked rulers at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because the fibre thickness might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a standard resting period. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
